title: Formal justifying act = practical fiducial assent to the whole Word, esp. Gospel promises
source_text: CXIII. Proinde meo judicio, nihil dici potest convenientius, quam actum formalem fidei salvificae & justificantis, qui proponitur tanquam salutis conditio, quo proxime disponimur ad justificationem, & per quem propterea Scriptura dicit nos justificari, nihil, inquam, convenientius dici potest, quam actum illum esse assensum practicum atque fiducialem adhibitum toti Dei Verbo, sed speciatim atque potissimum Evangelii promissionibus. Nam assensus ille practicus atque fiducialis sub se complectitur, & secum involvit omnes actus vivam & salvificam fidem constituentes: Et medium est a Deo destinatum per quod beneficiorum Christi participes simus; ac conditio illa cui Scriptura promittit remissionem peccatorum, & reliqua quibus constat hominis salus. Denique statim atque talis assensus in homine reperitur, propter Christum cessat esse irae divinae obnoxius, & incipit esse Deo gratus & acceptus ad vitam aeternam, quibus in rebus consistit hominis justificatio. Nec quisquam beneficiorum istorum particeps est, priusquam tali assensu praeditus sit.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore in my judgment nothing can be said more fittingly than that the formal act of saving and justifying faith, which is proposed as the condition of salvation, by which we are proximately disposed to justification, and through which therefore Scripture says we are justified — nothing, I say, can be said more fittingly than that that act is the practical and fiducial assent given to the whole Word of God, but specially and chiefly to the promises of the Gospel. For that practical and fiducial assent embraces under itself and involves with itself all the acts that constitute living and saving faith: And it is the means destined by God through which we become partakers of Christ's benefits; and that condition to which Scripture promises remission of sins, and the rest of which man's salvation consists. Finally, as soon as such assent is found in a person, because of Christ he ceases to be liable to divine wrath, and begins to be pleasing and acceptable to God unto eternal life, in which things man's justification consists. Nor is anyone partaker of those benefits before he is endowed with such assent.
pass_b_english: So the formal act of saving justifying faith — the condition by which we are proximately disposed to justification, and through which Scripture says we are justified — is best stated as practical fiducial assent to the whole Word of God, especially the Gospel promises.

That assent embraces every act that constitutes living saving faith; it is God's appointed means of sharing Christ's benefits and the condition to which Scripture attaches remission and the rest of salvation.

As soon as such assent is present, for Christ's sake one ceases to be under wrath and begins to be accepted to eternal life — which is justification itself. No one shares those benefits before that assent.
